messages:
Maya: Quick heads-up — a quantized HF-to-Redwood onboarding run (4-bit) is showing a clear quality regression on instruction benchmarks. Loss +6% vs fp16, coherence drops after ~600 tokens. Suspect conversion/config/tokenizer mismatch.
Liam: What part of the conversion changed? config.json, tokenizer, or quant pipeline logs?
Maya: No crash, model serves. But generated outputs insert an EOS in the middle sometimes. Traced to special token splitting: HF special token `<|assistant|>` became two tokens after our tokenizer serialization. Sliding-window logic then applied offsets incorrectly.
Derek: Token boundary shifts can shift KV cache alignment. Did you check num_key_value_heads and hidden_heads mapping in converted config?
Maya: HF had `num_key_value_heads: 32`, our converted `config.json` ended up with 16. Also noticed `max_position_embeddings` got truncated from 8192 -> 4096 during conversion because sliding_window defaulted the maxpos to window_size.
Sanjay: So we have at least two interacting issues: 1) special token tokenization split causing token index offsets, 2) kv-head mismatch, and 3) maxpos reduction triggering rope extrapolation. Any rope_scaling differences?
Maya: HF had no explicit rope_scaling. Conversion added `rope_scaling: {"mode":"linear","alpha":0.9}` by default. That plus reduced maxpos yields wrong interpolation for rotary embeddings past 4096.
Liam: That combination explains the hallucination/regression pattern — kv cache offsets wrong when tokens >4096, and rope scaling mismatches cause embeddings drift.
Derek: Quick repro: craft a deterministic prompt that forces >4096 tokens and compare kv cache indices / shapes between HF origin and converted model. Also test with tokenizer forced to treat special token as single token via `tokenizer.add_special_tokens({"additional_special_tokens": ["<|assistant|>"]})` before serializing.
Maya: Minimal snippet I used: 
```
# minimal check
tokens = tok.encode(prompt)
assert len(tokens) > 4096
kv_index = len(tokens) - 1
print(model.kv_cache.shape, "expected_kv_heads=32")
```
Observed kv_cache shape implies 16 kv heads, mismatch against expectation.
Sanjay: Proposed remediation steps:
1) Preserve HF `num_key_value_heads` during conversion; don't let quantization heuristics downscale it silently.
2) Preserve or explicitly copy `max_position_embeddings` from HF -> converted config; sliding_window should be a runtime strategy, not an implicit maxpos truncate.
3) Avoid injecting rope_scaling defaults unless HF defines them; add an explicit conversion flag `--preserve-rope` to keep HF behavior.
4) Ensure tokenizer special tokens are merged/added to `special_tokens_map` before serializing.
5) Re-run quant pipeline with `--preserve-params`/`--no-param-repack` and smoke evals.
Liam: Also add a unit test in conversion CI that diffs critical fields: ["rope_scaling","sliding_window","num_key_value_heads","max_position_embeddings","special_tokens_map"] and fails if altered without explicit flag.
Maya: I'll open a small PR to the conversion script implementing the preserve flags + test. Assigning @Derek for review. I also uploaded a dump of mismatched outputs to s3://redwood-onboard/1723456789-token-map-samples for eval tracking.
Derek: Will review today. Also can we include a simple quant smoke eval comparing fp16 vs 4-bit with identical tokenizer/config to isolate quantization-only regressions?
Maya: Yes — plan: 1) fix conversion to preserve fields, 2) re-run fp16 vs 4-bit with identical tokenizer/config, 3) run instructionbench/selfchat/rouge diffs and share results.
deploy-bot: CI triggered for branch maya/config-preserve (build #4122) :white_check_mark:
Maya: Thanks — will post updated eval numbers once CI passes and tests finish.
